hints: A tangent equation needs both the point on the curve and the derivative there.
Differentiate $y=x\cos2x$ by the product rule to get $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\cos2x-2x\sin2x$.
At $x=\tfrac\pi2$, evaluate both $y$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, then use the point-gradient form of a straight line.
walkthrough: Use the product rule correctly on $y=x\cos2x$, attempting $(dx/dx)\cos2x+x\,d(\cos2x)/dx$
Obtain a correct derivative such as $\cos2x-2x\sin2x$
Obtain $dy/dx=-1$ and $y=-\frac12\pi$ when $x=\frac12\pi$, following through their derivative as printed
Obtain $x+y=0$, or equivalent; both $y$ and $dy/dx$ at $x=\frac12\pi$ must be shown

ai_rubric.Finding Equations of Tangents: Applies the product rule on $y=x\cos2x$, $(dx/dx)\cos2x+x\,d(\cos2x)/dx$. Derives a derivative such as $\cos2x-2x\sin2x$. The final result is $x+y=0$.

skill_tags: Finding an Area Under a Curve

hints: The shaded area is the definite integral of $x\cos2x$ from the origin to its first positive $x$-intercept.
Solve $\cos2x=0$ to identify the upper limit $x=\tfrac\pi4$ shown in the diagram.
Integrate $\int x\cos2x\,dx$ by parts with $u=x$ and $dv=\cos2x\,dx$.
Evaluate $\tfrac12x\sin2x+\tfrac14\cos2x$ at $x=\tfrac\pi4$ and $x=0$, subtracting in the correct order.
walkthrough: Integrate by parts and reach a form $ax\sin2x+b\int\sin2x\,dx$
Complete the integration to obtain $\frac12x\sin2x+\frac14\cos2x$, or equivalent
Use limits $x=0$ and $x=\frac\pi4$ in the correct order after integrating twice to an expression $ax\sin2x+c\cos2x$; allow at most one substitution error
Obtain $\frac\pi8-\frac14$, or an exact simplified two-term equivalent; accept $(\pi-2)/8$

ai_rubric.Finding an Area Under a Curve: Integrates by parts and reaches a form $ax\sin2x+b\int\sin2x\,dx$. Completes the integration to derive $\frac12x\sin2x+\frac14\cos2x$, or equivalent. The final result is $\dfrac\pi8-\dfrac14$.
